children: shares rose 2.98% intraday after the company said it reached a $131.5 million settlement with New York City's Department of Consumer and Worker Protection over findings that it underpaid workers or paid them late. The stock's gain alongside a settlement of that size suggests the market read the resolution as clearing an overhang.

The settlement includes nearly $115 million in relief for about 264,000 delivery workers and a $16.7 million fine. Of that relief, $83 million resolves a dispute over how to pay workers logged into the app and on-call but not actively delivering, and $12.3 million covers payments that were missed or arrived late. DoorDash put its median payout at about $48 and said it has fixed the technical issues behind the errors, which it attributed to cross-boundary deliveries, multi-stop orders, canceled trips, software bugs, and incomplete banking details.

The city accused both DoorDash and Uber Eats (UBER) of "design tricks" that withheld more than $550 million in tips, and Uber's share of the probe is unresolved. DoorDash, Uber Eats, and Grubhub have repeatedly clashed with New York over its tipping laws and data-sharing rules.

title: DoorDash Stock Rises After $131.5 Million NYC Settlement
